title: The quiet giants of the pavement
text: Japan has roughly one vending machine for every thirty people — some four million of them {{1}} in pavements, station platforms and temple car parks, selling everything from hot corn soup to fresh flowers and, famously, second-hand books. The {{2}} is partly practical: labour costs are high, rents for a machine are a {{3}} of those for a shop, and crime is low enough that machines survive unguarded all night. The results are {{4}} efficient: machines work around the clock, never call in sick, and {{5}} to tastes with an intimacy no chain store can match — hot drinks in winter, cold in summer, with the same machine {{6}} between the two at the press of a button. Operators {{7}} their restocking routes by data, sending drivers only where sensors report sales. The {{8}} is the energy bill: four million fridges and heaters idling round the clock, which is why the industry has spent a decade on insulation and sensors that let machines sleep when the street is empty. What looks like street furniture is, in fact, one of the most finely tuned retail networks on earth.

gaps.explanation: 'four million of them clustered in pavements' — gathered in tight groups; cobble = pave or patch together roughly.
'the ubiquity is partly practical' — their presence everywhere has practical causes; intricacy = complex detail.

gaps.hint: a tiny part (a ___ of those for a shop)
gaps.explanation: 'rents are a fraction of those for a shop' — a small share of them; faction = a group within a larger one.
'the results are spectacularly efficient' — impressively so; sporadically = at irregular intervals.
'machines respond to tastes' — react and adapt to them; redound takes 'to' but means contribute to credit.
'the same machine flipping between the two' — changing from hot to cold; flank = stand at the side of.
'operators optimise their restocking routes' — make them maximally efficient; ostracise = exclude from a group.
'the downside is the energy bill' — the negative aspect; downturn = a fall in business activity, downpour = heavy rain.
